long_biography.plain_text:
At the University of Tulsa, Arthur “Chip” McElroy II helped give engineering students a place to turn drawings into working parts. His family funded the McElroy Prototyping Laboratory, equipped with a computer-controlled mill and lathe. The McElroy Manufacturing chief, who had worked as a draftsman and engineer before leading the company, wanted graduates to be able to build what they designed.

McElroy’s support for young people also extends to Scouting. An Eagle Scout himself, he joined the Indian Nations Council’s board in 1995 and later served as council president. He has also worked with his wife and sisters to endow University of Tulsa scholarships, including one established in his father’s memory.
